help.name: A name so you recognise the loan, for example "DNB mortgage". Only you see it.
help.category: Pick what kind of loan it is, and the app suggests usual values and a typical rate right now.
help.amount: The amount you originally borrowed. It's in the loan agreement or your online bank as "original loan amount". If you don't have it, use today's balance.
help.rate: The rate the bank charges, also called the nominal or floating rate. It's in your online bank. Don't use the effective rate here.
help.effective: The effective rate is the nominal rate plus fees, expressed as one yearly percentage. The bank states it. Fill it in to check that your fees add up.
help.term: How long the loan runs in total, from start to the last payment. It's in the loan agreement. Mortgages are often 25–30 years, car loans 5–7.
help.type: Annuity: the same amount every month, mostly interest at first. Serial: equal principal payments, so the payment starts high and falls. Most mortgages are annuity loans.
help.intro: Some loans start with interest-only years, where you pay only interest, or interest-free years at 0 %. It's in the loan agreement.
help.startDate: The date the loan started. Pick the same day of the month as you pay, so payments land on the right day. Used to show how far you've come.
help.remaining: How much you owe today. It's in your online bank as "balance" or "current loan amount". Leave it empty to work it out from the plan.
help.fee: The fee added to every bill. It's on your invoice or in the loan agreement, often 0–100 kr.
help.setupFee: The one-off fee when the loan was set up, often plus a registration fee. It only affects total cost and the effective rate.
help.dayCount: How the bank counts interest days. Most floating-rate loans use actual days (365/365). It's in the loan terms. If unsure, leave it.
help.extras: An extra payment that goes straight to the debt. Your payment stays the same, but the loan ends sooner and you pay less interest.
help.goal: Pick when you want to be done, and the app works out how much extra you need to pay each month, or as one lump sum.
help.periods: Periods that differ from the plan: interest-only, where you pay just interest, or another rate, such as 0 % or a fixed-rate period.
help.after: After an interest-only period the bank either keeps the end date, so the payment goes up, or keeps the payment, so the loan runs longer.

q.effective: What is the effective rate, and why does mine match the bank's or not?
q.dayCount: What does the day count mean, and which should I choose?
q.remaining: Where do I find the remaining balance, and what happens if I leave it empty?
q.intro: What's the difference between an interest-only and an interest-free start, and what does it mean for my loan?
q.gap: The effective rate from my numbers doesn't match the bank's. What's missing?

rates.q: What is the difference between the nominal and the effective rate?
rates.a: The nominal rate is what the bank charges on your balance. The effective rate also includes fees and monthly compounding, and shows what the loan really costs per year. Compare offers on the effective rate, and enter both in the calculator so it can check that the fees add up.

extra.q: Is it worth paying extra on my loan?
extra.a: Every extra krone goes straight to the balance, so you stop paying interest on it for the rest of the loan. The calculator shows how much interest you save and how much sooner the loan is paid off, for a monthly amount or a one-off payment. Keep a savings buffer before paying extra.

interestOnly.q: What does an interest-only period mean?
interestOnly.a: During an interest-only period you pay only interest and fees. The balance does not go down, so the loan costs more in total or the payment is higher afterwards. Add the period under "Periods" to see what it costs you.

type.q: Annuity or serial loan: what is the difference?
type.a: An annuity loan has the same payment every month, with mostly interest at first. A serial loan repays the same principal every month, so payments start higher and fall, and you pay less interest in total. Switch the loan type in the calculator to see the difference for your loan.

finishBy.q: How much must I pay to finish my loan by a certain year?
finishBy.a: Choose "Done by" and a year. The calculator works out the extra monthly amount, or the one-off payment, that finishes the loan by then.

startlan.a: A startlån is a loan from the municipality for people who cannot borrow enough from a bank. It often runs for a long time, up to 50 years, and may start with a period without repayments. Choose "Startlån" as the loan type to fill in the usual terms.

method.a: It works month by month the way banks do: annuity or serial, interest on actual days (365/365) or equal months (30/360), monthly fee and setup fee. The figures are estimates. Your bank's figures are the ones that count.

privacy.a: No. What you enter stays in your own browser, with no account or sign-in. We count anonymous visits without cookies. If you use "Ask AI", your question and the loan figures, but not the loan's name, are sent to OpenAI to write the answer.

compareHow.q: How do I compare two loan offers?
compareHow.a: Look at the total cost, not just the rate. An offer with a lower rate can cost more if its fees are higher. Enter amount, rate, term and fees for both offers, and the page shows total cost, payment and effective rate side by side.

switch.q: When does it pay to switch banks?
switch.a: It pays when the interest you save is more than the switch costs, such as setup and registration fees. Under "Switch bank?" you see the total saving and how many months it takes to earn back the cost.

ratesPage.meaningTitle: What does the average mean for you?
ratesPage.meaning1: The average is the rate people actually got on new mortgages that month. Your own rate may be lower or higher, depending among other things on how much you borrow compared with the home's value, and on the bank.
ratesPage.meaning2: If your rate is well above the average, it may pay to ask your bank for a better offer or compare other banks.
